title: Technical interview skill matrix and first 30-day ramp plan — Eng ICs (satellite team onboarding)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact hiring + onboarding artifact intended to serve two related use cases for small satellite engineering teams: 1) a concise technical interview skill matrix and calibration guide for interviewers, and 2) a pragmatic, day-by-day first 30-day ramp checklist a manager and buddy can follow.

Why this exists (context):
- We frequently hire mid-senior ICs into small satellite teams (3–6 engineers) where production-readiness and independent execution matter more than large-system design.
- Existing rubrics are either too heavyweight (full-stack enterprise templates) or too vague. This doc aims to be interviewer-friendly (one page when printed) and actionable for first-30-days planning.
- Drafted after calibration sessions with Eng Managers (Ethan, Marisol) and SRE (Liam).

Part A — Technical interview skill matrix (for calibration / scorecards)
Scoring conventions: 1 = does not meet bar, 3 = meets expectations for level, 5 = exceeds expectations (clear leadership/mentorship signal). For hiring decisions, look at distribution across categories rather than a single total.

Categories (short descriptions + interviewer prompts + example evidence):
1) Core coding (algorithms, data structures) — prompt: "Implement a rate limiter / dedupe stream"
   - Evidence: clear approach, justified complexity, test cases, handles edge cases.
   - Notes: For mid-senior ICs we accept pragmatic, readable solutions (O(N log N) ok if tradeoffs discussed).

2) Production design & reliability — prompt: "Design a request routing fallback when model variants are down"
   - Evidence: tradeoffs (latency vs correctness), deployment and rollback considerations, metrics to monitor (tail latency, error budget), and runbook thought.

3) Observability & debugging — prompt: "You get paged with tokenization mismatch increasing error rate — how do you triage?"
   - Evidence: clear hypothesis-driven steps, use of logs/traces/metrics, minimal repro.

4) System/component ownership & shipping velocity — prompt: "Describe a recent bug you took to production and how you prevented recurrence."
   - Evidence: release plan, test coverage added, automation, documentation.

5) Communication & cross-team collaboration — prompt: "How do you align with product & infra when shipping a model change?"
   - Evidence: examples of stakeholder mapping, written notes, design docs + async updates.

6) Cultural fit / psychological safety — prompt: "Tell us about a time you disagreed with a team decision."
   - Evidence: respectful challenge, evidence-based persuasion, work to resolution.

Interviewer guidance (calibration bullets):
- Use concrete examples from candidates — avoid hypotheticals-only answers.
- If unsure between two scores, default to the lower score and flag to hiring manager; we prefer conservative calibration.
- Panel owners must submit a short summary line (1–2 sentences) explaining the decisive factor.
- Must-not-do: judge solely on language, university, or micro-tic.

Sample short scorecard template (for interviewer notes):
- Candidate: __________
- Role/Level: __________
- Core coding: 1–5 -> evidence line
- Prod design: 1–5 -> evidence line
- Observability/debugging: 1–5 -> evidence line
- Ownership/shipping: 1–5 -> evidence line
- Communication/culture: 1–5 -> evidence line
- Hiring recommendation: Strong Yes | Yes | Consider | No

Part B — First 30-day ramp plan (satellite team focused)
How to use this: manager prints this and shares with new hire + buddy during offer acceptance. This is expected to be adapted to team-specific milestones (feature launch, bug backlog, etc.).

Key success metrics for day 30 (examples):
- Has a reproducible dev environment and can run the main service locally or in dev cluster.
- Has shipped at least one small, owner-identified change (bugfix, test, doc) through the full cycle.
- Can independently triage a simple production alert with the buddy present.
- Contributed to a short retrospective or learned-items doc.

Week 0 (pre-start checklist — HR + manager):
- Accesses granted: GitHub, CI, dev VPN, internal docs. (HR to confirm before day 1)
- Buddy assigned and intro Slack message scheduled.
- Small starter ticket created and labeled FIRST-CHANGE.

Day 1–3 (orientation + access):
- Day 1: 1:1 with manager (roles, expectations, current team OKRs), meet team standup.
- Day 2: Pair with buddy to build/run local dev environment; smoke test service.
- Day 3: Walkthrough of deployed infra, monitoring dashboards (what to watch), and common runbooks.

Day 4–10 (discover & small ship):
- Pick FIRST-CHANGE ticket (small bug/documentation) and complete code review cycle.
- Sit on on-call rotations in observation mode (no solo pages).
- Read 2–3 key design docs (links provided).
- End-week: write a 1-page ramp note: what’s confusing, quick wins, open questions.

Week 2 (ownership & integration):
- Begin owning a subcomponent or ticket board column (e.g., inference adapters, cache invalidation).
- Deliver a small feature or performance test and present results in a short demo.
- Schedule a 30-min sync with product partner to understand roadmap priorities.

Week 3 (independent shipping + observability):
- Lead a small incident replay (postmortem writeup practice).
- Add one meaningful dashboard or alert improvement.
- Mentor: shadow a buddy doing a design review, then provide one written comment.

Week 4 (solidify & reflect):
- Ship a slightly larger improvement that touches infra or telemetry.
- Present 15-min "what I learned" at team retro.
- Manager: evaluate against day-30 metrics and set 60–90 day goals.

Manager checklist (deliverables and signals):
- Verify access, buddy assignment, and FIRST-CHANGE ticket pre-created.
- Weekly 1:1 scheduled for first 60 days (30, 45, 60).
- Make time for a 30-min calibration review of interview feedback (if hire was recent).

Buddy checklist (day-to-day):
- First week: pair 2–4 hours/day until local env stable.
- Maintain a 1-page living notes doc for the hire (links, gotchas, useful commands).
- Be available for quick 20–30m troubleshooting sessions.

Triage playbook (short):
- If paged: confirm scope, check runbooks, gather logs/traces, escalate to on-call SRE if unclear.
- Document steps taken in incident channel and create follow-up tasks before end of day.

Open questions / to resolve in next iteration:
- Should we require a short take-home for senior infra candidates? (pros/cons list below — need People Ops+Hiring Managers call)
- How to adjust scoring weights for Levels 4 vs 5 (ownership vs system design emphasis).

Notes to self / operational reminders:
- Keep the matrix printable on one page — panels often want short prompts.
- Pull common candidate answers into a calibration doc on Confluence to speed interviewer prep.

References and quick links:
- Primary onboarding framework: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HR/eng-onboarding-framework
- Starter ticket template: REPO: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/FIRST-CHANGE.md (link on Confluence)
- Hiring JIRA board: JIRA: RECRUIT-919

If you’re reviewing this doc: please add one-line feedback to the bottom (what’s missing or too heavy).
